description: "We are a team of passionate problem-solvers and tech enthusiasts participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge to build innovative solutions for real-world Earth and space challenges. Combining data analysis, creative design, and critical thinking, our goal is to turn complex scientific challenges into practical, impact-driven tools."
summary:
Project Summary
Earth Twins is an interactive educational web app that shows how places on Earth help us understand the Moon and Mars. Many Earth locations are scientific "analogs": they share climate, geology, and minerals with places on other worlds. The app pairs four of them: the Atacama Desert with Gale Crater, Lake Salda with Jezero Crater, Death Valley with Holden Crater, and the McMurdo Dry Valleys with the Lunar South Pole.
Users explore a 3D Earth, choose a location, and see it side by side with its twin in a split-screen 3D view. They compare weather, geology, and minerals. A younger-audience mode (under 12) explains each place in simple words with a landing experience. The older mode (12+) gives technical descriptions and ends with a mission game, where players fight aliens, collect clues, and guess which Earth location the clues describe.
Our goal is to make planetary science fun and show that exploring space can start right here on Earth.
